name: Agent Assurance — DAG-TOML Specification
description: DAG-TOML is a public specification for describing how software agents plan work, sequence dependencies, cite evidence, declare their abstraction boundaries, and prove readiness for human review. It is intentionally a data format, not an execution runtime.
homepage_url_justification: https://agent-assurance.dev — project homepage published as a static site (GitHub Pages backed); served exclusively over HTTPS.
sites_https_justification: Both https://agent-assurance.dev and https://github.com/verivus-oss/agent-assurance enforce HTTPS via HSTS. There are no project-controlled non-HTTPS URLs.
description_good_justification: Homepage hero (https://agent-assurance.dev) reads: 'DAG-TOML proves what an agent intended, depended on, and made ready for review.' followed by 'A TOML format for declarative policy, workflow, traceability, evidence, closure roots, and review gates in agent-driven software development.' The Positioning section then explains the three roles in plain English (Declares intent / Preserves provenance / Stays runtime-neutral). README.md lines 7-32 carry the same text in repo-readable form. A reader can understand what DAG-TOML is, who uses it, and what problem it solves within the first 32 lines without specialist vocabulary.
interact_justification: Homepage hero links to https://github.com/verivus-oss/agent-assurance for collaboration. GitHub Issues is enabled (https://github.com/verivus-oss/agent-assurance/issues), GitHub Discussions is enabled, security reports go to security@verivus.com per SECURITY.md, and CONTRIBUTING.md (https://github.com/verivus-oss/agent-assurance/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) describes how to contribute. Issue templates live in .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/.
contribution_justification: https://github.com/verivus-oss/agent-assurance/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md explains the contribution process (Fast Path, Good Issues, Spec Change Process, Review Discipline, Local Checks, Style, Licensing).
contribution_requirements_justification: https://github.com/verivus-oss/agent-assurance/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md lists the requirements for acceptable contributions: Spec Change Process section requires that a PR reference an issue, update prose AND matching *-kind.toml descriptors together, update ontology files when relation vocabulary changes, add/update examples on file-shape change, update CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased], and pass the reference validators. The Style section lists the coding/style requirements (normative MUST/SHOULD/MAY, minimal executable examples, kebab-case template_kind values, prefixed IDs, two-space TOML indentation). Licensing section requires Apache-2.0 acceptance.
documentation_basics_justification: README.md provides a role-based 'Start Here' navigation (https://github.com/verivus-oss/agent-assurance/blob/main/README.md#start-here) routing readers to spec.md, docs/field-reference.md, docs/architecture.md, validators, examples, and profile overviews. spec.md is the normative specification. profiles/agent-assurance/overview.md and profiles/agent-assurance/tiers/README.md cover the optional Agent Assurance Profile.
documentation_interface_justification: The 'interface' of a specification project is the spec itself plus the per-kind contracts. spec.md (https://github.com/verivus-oss/agent-assurance/blob/main/spec.md) is the normative file-format specification. core/*-kind.toml and profiles/*/<kind>-kind.toml carry the machine-readable per-kind contracts. docs/field-reference.md provides field-level documentation. docs/architecture.md documents the runtime/non-runtime boundary.
discussion_justification: GitHub Issues is enabled (https://github.com/verivus-oss/agent-assurance/issues, has_issues=true) and GitHub Discussions is enabled (has_discussions=true). Both support threaded discussion.
english_justification: README.md, spec.md, docs/, CHANGELOG.md, SECURITY.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, GOVERNANCE.md, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, SUPPORT.md, AGENTS.md, and all *-kind.toml descriptors are written in English.
maintained_justification: Recent merge activity 2026-05-27: PRs #8, #9, #10, #11 all merged. Active [Unreleased] section in CHANGELOG.md documents incremental improvements. The signing-approvers team (verivus-open, verivusOSS-releases, plus a human reviewer per CODEOWNERS) is the named maintainer set.
repo_track_justification: Git repository tracks all changes; full history is publicly viewable at https://github.com/verivus-oss/agent-assurance/commits/main.
repo_interim_justification: Intermediate changes tracked via PR branches (e.g., PRs #8, #9, #10, #11 are recent examples) and Dependabot's dependabot/* branches.
repo_distributed_justification: Git is a distributed version-control system. Anyone can clone https://github.com/verivus-oss/agent-assurance.git.
version_unique_justification: Released versions use unique, monotonic identifiers. v0.1.0 is the only release; future releases will follow vX.Y.Z semver or calendar-versioned UTC tags per GOVERNANCE.md.
version_semver_justification: v0.1.0 follows Semantic Versioning. GOVERNANCE.md (https://github.com/verivus-oss/agent-assurance/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#releases) documents the version-pin policy. README.md status table records the schema_version semver pin.
version_tags_justification: Releases use Git annotated tags. v0.1.0 (https://github.com/verivus-oss/agent-assurance/releases/tag/v0.1.0) is an annotated, sigstore-signed tag.
release_notes_justification: Release notes ship with each release. https://github.com/verivus-oss/agent-assurance/releases/tag/v0.1.0 carries the v0.1.0 release notes. CHANGELOG.md follows the Keep-a-Changelog format and the [Unreleased] section tracks incremental change.
release_notes_vulns_justification: SECURITY.md Disclosure section (https://github.com/verivus-oss/agent-assurance/blob/main/SECURITY.md#disclosure) commits to crediting reporters in CHANGELOG.md for the release that fixes a finding. No known vulnerabilities fixed yet (project minted 2026-05-27); the documented process is ready.
report_tracker_justification: GitHub Issues is the bug tracker. Issue templates live in .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/.
report_process_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md 'Good Issues' section (https://github.com/verivus-oss/agent-assurance/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#good-issues) describes the issue-reporting process. SECURITY.md covers the vulnerability-report process.
report_responses_justification: SECURITY.md commits to acknowledging reports within five business days. CONTRIBUTING.md establishes the maintainer-review path.
enhancement_responses_justification: GOVERNANCE.md 'Decision Types' table (https://github.com/verivus-oss/agent-assurance/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#decision-types) lists the required path for each change type. 'Review Expectations' commits maintainers to reviewable-in-one-sitting responses.
report_archive_justification: Public archive of reports and responses, searchable: https://github.com/verivus-oss/agent-assurance/issues?q=is%3Aissue (issues, open and closed); https://github.com/verivus-oss/agent-assurance/discussions (discussions, all categories); https://github.com/verivus-oss/agent-assurance/pulls?q=is%3Apr (pull requests, open and closed). Repo-wide search at https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Averivus-oss%2Fagent-assurance&type=issues. All threads — including closed ones — are retained indefinitely by GitHub and remain publicly viewable.
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY.md Reporting section (https://github.com/verivus-oss/agent-assurance/blob/main/SECURITY.md) documents the vulnerability-report process: email security@verivus.com with a short description, minimal reproduction, and scope statement. GitHub's native private vulnerability reporting is also enabled.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: Two private channels for vulnerability reports. (1) Email security@verivus.com, documented at https://github.com/verivus-oss/agent-assurance/blob/main/SECURITY.md (Reporting a vulnerability section, lines 3-15) — acknowledgement within five business days; default 30-day disclosure embargo. (2) GitHub Private Vulnerability Reporting (PVR) — end-to-end-private form submission via https://github.com/verivus-oss/agent-assurance/security/advisories/new (Report a vulnerability button in the repository Security tab). Both channels are private: email is point-to-point to a maintainer-controlled inbox; GitHub PVR is audit-logged inside the Security tab and never visible to non-maintainers.
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: SECURITY.md commits to acknowledgement within five business days. No vulnerability reports filed yet (project minted 2026-05-27); documented process is ready.
build_justification: DAG-TOML is a specification (TOML + Markdown). There is no build step for the spec itself; reference validators under tools/ are non-normative implementer guidance, not the project's deliverable.
build_common_tools_justification: See build_status — no build for the spec itself. Reference validators under tools/dagtoml-validate-rs/ (cargo) and tools/dagtoml-validate-go/ (go) use common build tools, documented in README.md.
build_floss_tools_justification: See build_status — no build for the spec itself. Reference validators use cargo (Apache/MIT) and go (BSD); Taplo CLI (MIT/Apache) — all FLOSS.
test_justification: CI runs reference validators against canonical examples on every push and pull request. .github/workflows/validate.yml invokes the Rust and Go primary validators plus Python cross-checks against every canonical example, tier file, profile descriptor, and ontology. Local invocation documented in README.md 'Local Validation' section and CONTRIBUTING.md 'Local Checks' section.
test_invocation_justification: README.md 'Local Validation' section (https://github.com/verivus-oss/agent-assurance/blob/main/README.md#local-validation) lists the canonical local-invocation commands. CONTRIBUTING.md 'Local Checks' section shows individual validator commands.
test_most_justification: Reference validators have parser-conformance tests against the upstream toml-test suite (Rust + Go variants). The spec's invariants (graph-shaped rules, IJB conformance, closure-root, abstraction-class, kind-descriptor structural rules) all have validator coverage exercised by .github/workflows/validate.yml.
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md 'Spec Change Process' section requires that PRs 'Pass the reference validators' and 'Add or update at least one example when the file shape changes'.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitHub Actions runs .github/workflows/validate.yml on every push and pull request to main. https://github.com/verivus-oss/agent-assurance/actions/workflows/validate.yml shows the run history.
tests_are_added_justification: Examples (which act as tests for the validators) are added with new kinds. README.md states: 'A PR that changes a template_kind MUST update the matching *-kind.toml descriptor, the ontology entries it references, and the affected example under examples/ in the same change.' Reviewable via git log -- examples/ history.
tests_documented_added_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md documents the requirement; CI fails the build if examples are missing or invalid. The 'Verify no banned markers' and 'Verify documented examples exist' steps in validate.yml enforce this directly.
warnings_justification: Thirteen OSS scanners (actionlint, zizmor, shellcheck, typos, ruff, bandit, osv-scanner, gitleaks, cargo-audit, cargo-deny, govulncheck, golangci-lint, lychee) configured to fail the build on any finding. See SECURITY.md 'Thirteen OSS scanning tools in CI' section for the inventory and roles. Cargo builds use --locked. Pip installs use --require-hashes against checked-in lock files (requirements/{bandit,ruff,zizmor}.txt).
warnings_fixed_justification: All 13 scanners run continue-on-error: false and fail the build on any finding. Branch protection requires main to be green. Latest main runs show all 13 tools passing.
warnings_strict_justification: The 13-tool scanner block is layered defense-in-depth above GitHub-native security (CodeQL advanced-setup over 4 languages, secret scanning + push protection, Dependabot security updates). cargo-deny, cargo-audit, govulncheck, osv-scanner, and bandit enforce strict policies on dependencies and code. ruff includes Bandit S-rules. CodeQL runs queries: security-and-quality on actions/go/python/rust.
know_secure_design_justification: The project's designer (Werner Kasselman / verivusOSS-releases) authored the corrective-program design that produced the current branch-protection + signing-approver + sigstore-signed-tag posture. SECURITY.md 'Defensive posture' section documents the design. CONTRIBUTING.md 'Review Discipline' section documents the no-self-approval and closure-root invariants. tools/review-request-dag.toml encodes the multi-LLM independent-review workflow. The implementation evidences familiarity with secure-design principles.
know_common_errors_justification: The defensive posture addresses common-error classes explicitly: supply-chain via SHA-pinned actions, pip-hash-pinning, cargo-deny, Dependabot; secret leakage via gitleaks + push-protection; injection via actionlint shell-injection rules + zizmor impostor-commit audit; static-analysis blind spots via CodeQL advanced-setup over four languages; weak crypto via sigstore for releases.
crypto_published_justification: The DAG-TOML specification does not define cryptographic algorithms. Where SHA-256 is used (closure-root computation per spec.md §12), the algorithm is FIPS 180-4 (published). Sigstore (used for tag signing) uses published ECDSA P-256.
crypto_call_justification: Where SHA-256 is used (tools/dagtoml-validate-rs/ and tools/dagtoml-validate-go/), it is called from standard library or audited crates (sha2 Rust crate, crypto/sha256 in Go stdlib).
crypto_floss_justification: SHA-256 implementations used (sha2 Rust crate, Go stdlib) are FLOSS.
crypto_keylength_justification: No key-based crypto in the spec. Sigstore uses ECDSA P-256 (256-bit, ≥ 112-bit security per NIST SP 800-57).
crypto_working_justification: No broken cryptographic primitives used. SHA-256 (closure-root) and ECDSA P-256 (sigstore) are not broken.
crypto_pfs_justification: Project does not establish encrypted channels (no network protocol).
crypto_random_justification: Project does not generate cryptographic random values in the spec. Sigstore tag-signing uses a Fulcio-issued ephemeral key; randomness is sigstore's responsibility.
delivery_mitm_justification: Repo, release tarballs, and homepage are served exclusively over HTTPS by github.com / GitHub Pages. Annotated tags are sigstore-signed; verification via 'gitsign verify v0.1.0' against the public Rekor transparency log.
delivery_unsigned_justification: Release artifacts (v0.1.0 tag) are cryptographically signed via sigstore (gitsign). The signature lives in the annotated tag object; certificate SAN is oss-release@verivus.com. Verification instructions in SECURITY.md.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No known unpatched vulnerabilities. Dependabot view shows 0 open security alerts. CodeQL reports 0 critical open alerts after the post-merge re-scan. osv-scanner, cargo-audit, govulncheck all green in CI.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: Zero open critical vulnerabilities. Dependabot security updates enabled (weekly cadence). SECURITY.md documents the private-disclosure path.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: Secret scanning + push protection both enabled at the GitHub level. gitleaks runs in CI on every push (.github/workflows/validate.yml). Trailer-check invariant verified clean.
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL advanced-setup scans actions/go/python/rust on every push, every PR, and weekly (.github/workflows/codeql.yml). bandit runs Python static security analysis. ruff runs Python correctness + security S rules. gosec runs via golangci-lint meta-linter. cargo-deny enforces Rust license/ban/advisory policy. zizmor audits the workflow files themselves.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL security-and-quality query suite (configured in codeql.yml) covers OWASP/CWE Top 25 for each of the four languages. Bandit covers Python-specific security patterns. govulncheck covers Go's known-vuln callgraph. cargo-audit covers RustSec advisories.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: Branch protection ruleset main-branch-protection enforces validate.yml passing on main. Any finding from the 13-tool block fails the build. Latest main is green; all prior findings have been resolved as commits.
static_analysis_often_justification: Static analysis runs on every push and pull request. CodeQL additionally runs weekly via cron. OpenSSF Scorecard runs weekly.
dynamic_analysis_justification: Project deliverable is a TOML data format + Markdown prose specification, not executable code; there is no production runtime to dynamically analyze. Reference validators under tools/ (Rust + Go) are non-normative implementer guidance, not the project's deliverable, and they themselves run only in CI under static-analysis coverage (CodeQL, cargo-audit, govulncheck, etc.). Note: this criterion is category SUGGESTED at the Passing level and does not block the badge.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: Project does not include software written in memory-unsafe languages. Reference validators are written in safe-Rust (#![forbid(unsafe_code)] declared at the top of tools/dagtoml-validate-rs/src/main.rs) and safe-Go (no `unsafe` import; enforced by the 'Safe-tools policy (no unsafe Rust or Go under tools/)' step in .github/workflows/validate.yml). Python validators are also memory-safe. The conditional precondition of this criterion (memory-unsafe-language code) is not triggered.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: The conditional precondition of this criterion — 'IF the software produced by the project includes software written using a memory-unsafe language (e.g., C or C++)' — is not satisfied. The project's software (TOML spec + Markdown + safe-Rust + safe-Go + Python) contains no memory-unsafe-language code (verified by the 'Safe-tools policy' step in validate.yml). Therefore the criterion is vacuously satisfied. Where the reference validators use assertions, they do so via Rust's `assert!`/`debug_assert!` macros and Go's testing assertions in their own test suites.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: See dynamic_analysis_status. No dynamic-analysis findings to fix.
hardening_justification: Site-level: HTTPS-only on github.com and agent-assurance.dev; HSTS enforced. Workflow-level: step-security/harden-runner audits egress on every job (.github/workflows/{validate,codeql,scorecard}.yml); all third-party actions SHA-pinned; pip hash-pinning across all CI installs; least-privilege workflow tokens with explicit permissions blocks; secret scanning + push protection; Dependabot security updates; main-branch-protection ruleset + classic branch protection; CODEOWNERS-routed review; sigstore-signed annotated tags.
